**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 15.1 already contains a robust MSL-side (vendor) indemnity running in our favour:

- **IP infringement** (15.1(a)): patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work and trade secret claims worldwide, covering MSL's performance and MSL-procured parts, processes, designs, deliverables and pre-existing materials — the core requirement of the rule.
- **Breach of law** (15.1(b)) and **warranty/support failures** (15.1(c)).
- **Narrow carve-outs** (p0263): only claims caused by IBM-selected names/marks, IBM's written specifications, or defective designs traceable to IBM-provided specifications — i.e. our own inputs, tighter than the fallback's usual modification/combination exclusions.
- **Standard procedure** (15.2): prompt notice, mutual cooperation, MSL control of defence with our right to participate at our own expense; MSL bears damages, settlements, costs and attorneys' fees, with its 15.2(b) cure options exercised at MSL's own expense and subject to continued specification/warranty compliance.
- **Direction check**: no reciprocal IBM indemnity for MSL's services exists (search for an IBM-granted indemnity returned nothing), and Appendix A item 5 adds a further MSL indemnity in IBM's favour for Microsoft code matters.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: there is no express data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct prong, and § 16.21 permits MSL to suspend supply where an infringement claim arises from IBM-specified designs (with IBM bearing its own cure costs). These are sub-elements short of the preferred wording rather than failures of a material term.
